prompt:
You are the prosecutor. Your job is to FALSIFY the claims below. For each claim, either:
(a) state a concrete scenario in which it is false, AND propose a minimal test or command
    that would demonstrate it; or (b) state you could not falsify it.
You may also raise NEW hypotheses about behaviour the change silently alters.
Every hypothesis must cite exact diff lines. No confidence numbers.
note: Hypotheses only. A hypothesis counts as a finding only after the evidence engine runs its test_sketch and it reproduces. Nothing here was executed.

attacks.scenario: A generated type kind is missing the attribute: the helper types nested in the composite resolver, or a type emitted from a template not edited here.
attacks.test_sketch: Regenerate all snapshot inputs, parse every output file with Roslyn, and assert every ClassDeclaration/StructDeclaration/EnumDeclaration emitted by the generator has the attribute (or sits under an attributed parent), reporting the exceptions.

attacks.scenario: The test passes with an attribute missing from a type, because it counts per file.
attacks.test_sketch: Mutation: delete one of the three attributed declarations in ResolverTemplate.cs (and its .tt text); run CodeCoverageExclusionTests and the resolver snapshot tests; record which go red.

cited_lines.quote: /// Verifies that every type emitted by the source generator is decorated with <c>ExcludeFromCodeCoverage</c>

attacks.scenario: The attribute exists on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework, so the guard removes decoration that would have compiled fine; or, if it truly is missing there, nothing proves the guarded output compiles.
attacks.test_sketch: Compile a generated formatter and resolver (from a snapshot) against netstandard2.0, net472 and net8.0 reference assemblies with and without the guard (#define NETSTANDARD2_0 for the first); inspect the compiler output for CS0246 on ExcludeFromCodeCoverage.
attacks.holds_if: without the guard, netstandard2.0 and net472 compile errors appear

cited_lines.quote: The attribute is not available on netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework, so it is only emitted where it exists.

attacks.scenario: The generated layout for nested generic types with constraints changed beyond the attribute, and exactly one snapshot encodes that.
attacks.test_sketch: For every .g.cs diff hunk, test against the regex ^\+(#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK|\s*\[global::System\.Diagnostics\.CodeAnalysis\.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage\]|#endif)$; list hunks that do not match and the files they are in.

attacks.scenario: .tt edited but .cs not regenerated, or the reverse, in one of the six pairs.
attacks.test_sketch: For each pair extract the attribute and #if lines from the .tt and from the string literals in the .cs and compare after unescaping \r\n.

attacks.scenario: The first README line is unconditional, the second narrows it: a reader of the first sentence alone is misled for the excluded targets.
attacks.test_sketch: Documentation review; executable half is P-2297-3.
attacks.falsified_if: owner requires the first sentence to carry the condition

cited_lines.quote: All generated formatters and resolvers are decorated with `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]`, so generated code does not skew code coverage reports.
The attribute is only emitted for targets where it is available (not `netstandard2.0` or .NET Framework).

attacks.scenario: A test resolves the InterfaceUnion directory, so its three untouched snapshots should have changed.
attacks.test_sketch: git grep for the directory name in tests excluding Resources; run the generation tests and see whether the InterfaceUnion snapshots are read.
attacks.falsified_if: a reference exists and the test passes anyway

attacks.scenario: A hand-written member in the user's partial resolver class disappears from the coverage report after the change.
attacks.test_sketch: Build a tiny project with [GeneratedMessagePackResolver] partial class R { public int Hand() => 1; }, run coverlet with a test that calls Hand(), and compare covered lines of R before and after the change.
attacks.holds_if: Hand() is excluded after the change

new_hypotheses.text: On the nested FormatterCache<T> and GetFormatterHelper types the attribute is redundant (excluded through the parent) and adds three lines to every resolver snapshot; harmless but part of the diff size.
new_hypotheses.test_sketch: None needed; report in the scale view.

new_hypotheses.text: The README note sits in the section about mixing generated and custom formatters, not near the generator options, so a reader looking for coverage will not find it.

cited_lines.quote: All generated formatters and resolvers are decorated with `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]`, so generated code does not skew code coverage reports.
